claims.text: About $249M of federal polymer obligations as awarded — $280M in 2025 dollars.
claims.source: USAspending.gov, place of performance, PIC-12; BLS CPI-U annual averages for the real column
claims.assert: abs(sum(r['amount'] for r in D['naics']) - 249_000_000) < 5_000_000 and abs(sum(r['real'] for r in D['naics']) - 280_000_000) < 6_000_000
claims.actual: (sum(r['amount'] for r in D['naics']), sum(r['real'] for r in D['naics']))
claims.falsified_if: USAspending restates an obligation, or the CPI table is extended and changes the base. NOTE: an earlier version of this page published only the nominal sum. Adding more than one year of dollars together without adjusting is a defect, not a style choice — the gap here is 12 percent.
claims.official_check: The first adjustment attempt returned +3% because fiscal 2026 was missing from the CPI table and was silently skipped by an 'if year in CPI' guard. A lookup that skips what it cannot find is the same failure mode as a dead code: it produces a plausible number instead of an error.

claims.text: All Other Rubber Product Manufacturing (326299) is the largest recipient industry, ahead of tire manufacturing.
claims.source: USAspending by NAICS, summed across fiscal years
claims.assert: sorted({c: sum(r['amount'] for r in D['naics'] if r['code']==c) for c in set(r['code'] for r in D['naics'])}.items(), key=lambda t: -t[1])[0][0] == '326299'
claims.actual: sorted({c: sum(r['amount'] for r in D['naics'] if r['code']==c) for c in set(r['code'] for r in D['naics'])}.items(), key=lambda t: -t[1])[:3]
claims.falsified_if: A large tire award lands, or a 326299 award is de-obligated. NOTE: 326211 leads in individual fiscal years (FY2025) while 326299 leads the eight-year total — a single-year check would reproduce the original error.

claims.text: Tire manufacturing is the second-largest recipient industry.
claims.assert: sorted({c: sum(r['amount'] for r in D['naics'] if r['code']==c) for c in set(r['code'] for r in D['naics'])}.items(), key=lambda t: -t[1])[1][0] == '326211'
claims.actual: sorted({c: sum(r['amount'] for r in D['naics'] if r['code']==c) for c in set(r['code'] for r in D['naics'])}.items(), key=lambda t: -t[1])[:3]
claims.falsified_if: Either of the top two codes moves. Paired with fed-top-naics so the ordering cannot silently swap.

claims.text: Inflation adjustment does not change which industry received the most.
claims.source: derived: nominal and real rankings compared across all NAICS codes
claims.assert: sorted({r['code'] for r in D['naics']}, key=lambda k: -sum(x['amount'] for x in D['naics'] if x['code'] == k))[:3] == sorted({r['code'] for r in D['naics']}, key=lambda k: -sum(x['real'] for x in D['naics'] if x['code'] == k))[:3]
claims.actual: (sorted({r['code'] for r in D['naics']}, key=lambda k: -sum(x['amount'] for x in D['naics'] if x['code'] == k))[:3], sorted({r['code'] for r in D['naics']}, key=lambda k: -sum(x['real'] for x in D['naics'] if x['code'] == k))[:3])
claims.falsified_if: The nominal and real top-three diverge. They agree today, which is why the 'largest recipient is not tire manufacturing' finding survives the adjustment — worth checking again whenever a new fiscal year lands.

claims.text: The page states that university and research awards are invisible to the NAICS view.
claims.source: USAspending NAICS filter is 325*/326* manufacturing; a university files under 61xxxx
claims.assert: 'excludes' in D['meta'] and 'NAICS' in D['meta']['excludes'] and 'invisible' in D['meta']['excludes'].lower()
claims.falsified_if: The excludes note is dropped from the meta, or the NAICS filter widens to include 61xxxx/5417xx. This is a STRUCTURAL absence, not a suppression: the NSF NEO-SMART Engine ($14,999,983) and TARDISS are real federal money in these counties that this view cannot see. An absence produced by a filter reads exactly like an absence in the world, which is why it has to be stated rather than noticed.
claims.official_check: The all-industry county rows DO capture these awards; only the NAICS rows exclude them. The two are shown separately and never summed.
